verses.1: Bilaad the Shukhite answered and said:
verses.2: How long will you keep talking like this? How long will your words be like a mighty wind?
verses.3: Does God distort justice? Does Shaddai twist what is right?
verses.4: If your children have sinned, He has handed them over to the consequences of their wrongdoing.
verses.5: If you would turn your heart toward God, and appeal to Shaddai,
verses.6: if you are innocent and upright, He will awaken you and restore your just portion.
verses.7: Your beginning will be marked by pain, but your end will be a great reward.
verses.8: Ask the generations of the past, search out the wisdom of your ancestors.
verses.9: For we are but yesterday and know nothing, our days are like a fleeting shadow on the ground.
verses.10: Will they not teach you? Will they not speak to you from the heart?
verses.11: Can a reed flourish without water? Can a willow grow without moisture?
verses.12: Still in its roots, it will not bear fruit before it is cut down, and before all the grass it withers.
verses.13: So it is with the paths of those who forget God; the hope of the wicked will perish.
verses.14: Their house is like the web of a spider, their security like a tent that a thief will tear down.
verses.15: They lean on their house, but it will not support them; they grasp it, but it will not endure.
verses.16: They are fresh in the morning, but by evening they are gone—like morning dew from the heat of the sun.
verses.17: Their roots cling to the rock, but they are like a bed of stones in the middle of the gravel.
verses.18: If it is uprooted from its place, or if it is crushed, then you will not see it.
verses.19: Indeed, the path of the wicked is pleasant, but from the dust another will grow.
verses.20: Indeed, God does not reject the innocent, nor does He delight in the power of evildoers.
verses.21: Until He fills your mouth with laughter and your lips with praise.
verses.22: Those who hate you will be clothed in shame, and the tents of the wicked will not exist.

notes:
Notes
- v. 18: "then you will not see it" — the Hebrew is somewhat ambiguous, but the context of destruction and non-existence supports this reading.
- v. 19: "the path of the wicked is pleasant" — the Hebrew uses a wordplay between the path of the wicked and the growth of a new plant from the earth, which is rendered to reflect the contrast.
